pattern.crimePattern: dairy farmer kills the milk grader who rejected her honest milk because she refused to pay bribes
pattern.notes: Fictional co-op. Lactometer grading at collection centres and grader corruption are real, widely discussed issues; readings follow the common published range. To be checked by the cultural reader.

ob.reportedBy: Peris Wanjugu, clerk, Kinangop Highland Dairy Co-op, Ol Kalou
ob.text: The clerk of Kinangop Highland Dairy Co-op reports that the co-op's milk grader, Dorothy Wangechi (33), was found dead at the grading table of the Ol Kalou collection centre at 11:20, after the morning collection.

facts.text: Dorothy Wangechi, milk grader, was found dead at the grading table of the Ol Kalou collection centre at 11:20.
Dorothy lies by the grading table, near the cooling tank. A dented 10-litre steel can is on the floor beside her.
The dented can is from the centre's rack. There are handprints on its base.
Grading book: Mary Amoit 1.029, 1.028, 1.030, all marked REJECTED. Zakayo Ndegwa 1.022, 1.023, 1.021, all marked ACCEPTED.
Wall chart: 'Normal whole milk reads 1.026–1.032. Below 1.026: water added.'
Dorothy's notebook, column 'B': 'Zakayo — 200 ✓' every day. 'Amoit — REFUSED' three days running.
Dorothy's phone: an incoming call at 10:05 from 'Mama Amoit', 1 minute 10 seconds.
Peris: she left at 10:00 to bank the morning's cash. Dorothy was fine, and alone. Peris found her at 11:20.
Peris's bank deposit slip is stamped 10:25 at the Ol Kalou branch; she queued from 10:10 to 10:40.
Peris: payments to farmers only go through the co-op ledger. Dorothy never lent to or borrowed from members.
Peris: last week the chairman, Hudson Karanja, shouted at Dorothy about "missing litres" in the totals.
Records, Mary's line: a call to Dorothy at 10:05.
Records: PesaPap, 10:16, KSh 100 to EZEKIEL NJUGUNA.
Records: Mary's phone in the collection-centre zone 10:20–10:40.
Ezekiel: he took Mary from her farm to the centre and dropped her at 10:20. "She was angry. She said she'd been robbed for three days."
Ezekiel rode off at 10:21 to another fare; a passenger paid him in Ol Kalou town at 10:34.
Maintenance log, Friday: the "missing litres" were a cooling-tank meter fault, now fixed.
Member map: Mary's and Dorothy's families farm on opposite sides of Ol Kalou. No shared boundary.
County dairy board minutes, Nyahururu: H. Karanja present 09:00–13:00.
David: his father was milking, then cutting fodder with him at home, 09:30–12:00.
Fingerprints taken from Mary Amoit in detention.
Autopsy: two blows with a heavy rounded rim, matching a milk can. No injury from a fall.
Autopsy: no fluid in the lungs; no marks on the neck.
Autopsy: death between 10:15 and 11:00.
Lab: Mary Amoit's prints are on the can's base, gripped upside down as if swung, not carried by the handle.
Toxicology: clean. No preservative, no poison.
Mary: "I delivered at half past six and went home. I didn't go back."
Mary: "That girl stole from me."
Mary admits she went back at about 10:20 to show Dorothy her milk was good. She says Dorothy laughed, "pay like everyone else", and she left her standing there.
Mary: "I never touched those cans. I brought my own."
Mary admits she took a can from the rack when Dorothy laughed.
Zakayo: "I was at home milking."
Zakayo admits he paid Dorothy 200 a day to pass his watered milk. "Everyone who waters pays."
Hudson: "I was in Nyahururu at the dairy board."

interrogations.intro: Mary is still in her milking clothes. "Dorothy? I delivered at half past six and went home."

topics.reply: One point zero two nine. That is good milk. Three days she poured it out in front of everyone.
I won't give my fingerprints. I'm not a thief.

interrogations.intro: Zakayo turns his cap round and round. "I bring my milk. I go home."

topics.reply: Yes, I paid her. Two hundred a day. Everyone who waters pays. I'm ashamed. I didn't hurt her.
Call my son. We were cutting fodder.

interrogations.intro: Hudson takes the call outside the dairy board. "Missing litres, yes, I shouted. It was the meter. We fixed it."

topics.reply: It was the cooling-tank meter. Fixed on Friday. Check the log.

interrogations.intro: Peris holds the bank deposit book against her chest. "I left at ten. She was fine. She was alone."

topics.reply: Mama Amoit? Her milk is always good. I didn't understand why it was rejected.

contradictions.reaction: I went back. To show her my milk was good. She laughed. She said, "Pay like everyone else." I left her standing there.
She looks at her hands for a long time. "...She laughed. I took a can from the rack. Three days of my milk on the floor. My daughter's fees."

No. Read her phone, then follow the boda.

prosecutor.pass: Two blows with a can rim. Yes.
fail: No fluid in the lungs. Not the tank.
Two blows, not a fall. Read the autopsy.

prosecutor.pass: Good milk poured away because she wouldn't pay. The court will understand. It will still convict.
fail: The missing litres were a meter fault. Try again.
Fear of exposure is the briber's problem, and he was at home.

proof.concludes: Mary's milk read 1.028–1.030, normal, yet was rejected; Zakayo's read 1.021–1.023, watered, yet was accepted, and he is ticked as paying "B". Mary refused to pay and lost three days' milk.

Mary said she never went back. She called Dorothy at 10:05, a boda dropped her at the centre at 10:20, and her phone stayed there until 10:40, inside the time of death and after the clerk had left. She admits it.
Her prints are on the base of the dented can, as if swung. Mary Amoit struck Dorothy with a steel milk can, because Dorothy rejected her honest milk when she refused to pay bribes.

eliminations.why: Hudson was at the dairy board in Nyahururu from 09:00 to 13:00.
Zakayo was milking and cutting fodder at home with his son from 09:30 to 12:00.
Peris was in the bank queue from 10:10 to 10:40; her slip is stamped 10:25.
Ezekiel rode off at 10:21 and was paid by another passenger in town at 10:34.
Two blows with a can rim, not a fall.
The "missing litres" were a meter fault, and that was the chairman's complaint.
That fear is Zakayo's, and he was at home.
They farm on opposite sides of Ol Kalou.
Dorothy never lent to or borrowed from members.

reconstruction.text: For a year Dorothy takes 200 shillings a day from farmers who water their milk. To keep the centre's average looking normal, she rejects honest milk from farmers who won't pay.
Mary won't pay. Three mornings her good milk reads 1.029 and is poured away. Three days' pay, and a school-fees loan that needs the deliveries.
10:05. She calls Dorothy to say she's coming. 10:20, a boda drops her at the centre. The clerk left at ten for the bank.
At the grading table Dorothy laughs: "Pay like everyone else." Mary takes a can from the rack, upside down, by its base.
She walks home through the mist at about 10:35. The grading book stays open at her name.

ui.beatNotes: Reading a scale against a reference: the grading book's numbers can be dragged onto the wall chart, and each reading snaps into "normal" or "watered". Small domain knowledge, given in-world, decides the case.
